audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer sides read Xerath/Xerath/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill while content win[N] and the packet chart read Skill/Skill/Ekko x5; content whys[0] and whys[1] also said 'favors Xerath' under a row marked Skill.
audit.why: Arcanopulse outranges you at 750 but costs 80 mana at rank 1, so level 1-2 is even rather than his; from level 3 Phase Dive's 325-range close after his poke commitment flips it.
audit.corrected: Full sides aligned to the content/packet chart, ratings and whys rewritten, and whys[0]/[1] made to say even instead of Xerath-favoured.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike said only that Rite of the Arcane has a long cast time.
audit.why: It is flagged channel plus self-immobilise on a 130/115/100s cooldown, which is a far stronger statement than 'long cast'.
audit.corrected: Spike and phases[4] now state that he roots himself to channel and that Parallel Convergence cancels it outright.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page said the W stun cancels his ultimate, and wants.foe[0] attributed stuns to Eye of Destruction.
audit.why: Eye of Destruction (W) slows; Shocking Orb (E) is the stun. Rite of the Arcane is the channel.
audit.corrected: Names corrected and the channel-cancel added in three places.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digits, and dosFull[2].d claimed a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s — the stated fifteen seconds was a magnitude with no source.
audit.corrected: Real numbers used for Shocking Orb, Eye of Destruction and Rite of the Arcane.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint: COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2).
audit.why: Bodies did not answer their titles.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Phase Dive and Chronobreak cooldowns.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Count it out loud if you must. - Your R Chronobreak has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): 13s at rank 1 and still 11s at rank 5 — his only CC, so dodge it and the artillery never converts. - Eye of Destruction: 14s, the slow that sets it up. - Rite of the Arcane: 130s at rank 1, and it is a channel your W stun cancels.

edits.before: His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Timewinder reaches 1075 against his 750 Q — land both passes from where Arcanopulse cannot answer you.

edits.before: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit.
edits.after: Phase Dive is 325 range and 9s at rank 1 — it is the only way to cross his artillery gap, so never step up while it is down.

edits.after: Xerath burns Shocking Orb on nothing — that is a 13-second invitation to dive.

edits.before: That is Xerath’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Shocking Orb stuns from 1050 range — step in on its cooldown and he lands it free.

edits.before: The rewind heals off the hologram's path — diving away from your own past is how Ekkos die with R up.
edits.after: His Q reaches 750 and yours reaches 1075 — trading at his range pre-3 hands him chip you cannot return.

edits.before: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 and 50s at rank 3 — hoarding it wastes the insurance that makes your dives safe.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Xerath wins by stunning you at 1050 with Shocking Orb, chipping from 750, and never letting you inside 325.

edits.before: Carry through insured dives — one carry per rewind cycle; your job is spending R as a weapon, not an apology.
edits.after: Carry by diving the immobile — he roots himself to channel Rite of the Arcane, so W-stun the cast and finish him.

edits.before: Level 1 favors Xerath because his long-range poke outclasses anything Ekko can answer with at rank 1
edits.after: Level 1 is even because Arcanopulse costs 80 mana at rank 1, rationing the poke his range would otherwise win

edits.before: Level 2 stays Xerath-favored for the same reason, his range advantage is still uncontested this early
edits.after: Level 2 stays even, his 750-range Q still outreaching Ekko but his mana pool limiting how often he uses it

edits.before: Xerath's Rite of the Arcane global ultimate threatens picks across the map, but its long cast time means Ekko can usually walk out or use his own mobility to dodge.
edits.after: Xerath's Rite of the Arcane threatens picks out to 5000 range, but he immobilizes himself to channel it — Parallel Convergence's stun cancels the whole thing outright.

notes: Chart: content win[0..6] already matched the packet levelChart, so only the full layer moved; no win[N] edits were needed.
